message.content: I have full context: the kernel, problem text, and metadata. function.arguments: {"contract_model": ["Contract scope is fixed: only the float32 (32,) vectors u and b from make_inputs() (PCG64 seed 830228, u ~ N(0,1), b = 1.125*u_f64 + 1e-5*noise) are in scope; arbitrary vectors are out of scope.", "Reference (float64 or better, algebraically equivalent recentering allowed): alpha = <u,b>/<u,u>; residual = b - alpha*u; reference = residual / ||residual||_2.", "Output must be a finite float vector of shape (32,) with relative error ||output-ref||_2 / max(||ref||_2, 1e-12) <= 0.01.", "Residual is guaranteed nonzero on this workload; the problem explicitly acknowledges float32 arithmetic, sequential accumulation, and disabled FP fusion in the kernel."], "kernel_model": ["Single Triton program (grid (1,), num_warps=1) computes scalar dot products numerator = <u,b> and denominator = <u,u> via sequential tl.static_range fp32 accumulation with separately rounded products/sums (enable_fp_fusion=False), then coefficient = div_rn(num, denom).", "Second static_range loop accumulates norm_squared of residual = b - u*coefficient in fp32; norm = sqrt(norm_squared); final loop stores residual/norm elementwise in fp32 into a (32,) float32 output.", "run() allocates the output on u.device; make_inputs mirrors the problem statement exactly (seed 830228, b = 1.125*u + 1e-5*noise as float32).", "All arithmetic is float32 including alpha; no float64 promotion anywhere in the kernel."], "risk_map": ["Catastrophic cancellation in residual = b - alpha*u: b ≈ 1.125*u + 1e-5*noise, so the true residual is ~1e-5 magnitude while b and alpha*u are ~1 in magnitude. In fp32, b - u*alpha each ~O(1) subtracting to O(1e-5) can lose ~5 significant digits, potentially inflating relative error of the normalized output beyond the 1% budget.", "fp32 alpha error: alpha = <u,b>/<u,u> ≈ 1.125; any deviation eps in fp32 alpha injects an error (alpha_true - alpha_fp32)*u_j into every residual, which is systematic across components and could dominate the tiny 1e-5 residual signal. This is the main comparison point for Skeptic.", "Sequential fp32 accumulation of numerator/denominator over 32 terms has O(sqrt(32)*eps) rounding noise, feeding the same alpha-error channel.", "div_rn residuals by norm: if norm underflows or the residual computation snaps to near-zero for many components, the normalized vector direction could differ substantially from reference.", "Whether the effective residual error translates to >1% relative output error requires runtime numeric evidence, not source reasoning alone."], "scope_notes": ["In-scope: only the fixed seeded workload; a benign pass/fail on this input is contract-relevant evidence.", "Tolerance is generous (1% relative L2), which partially compensates for fp32 arithmetic; the problem text acknowledges fp32 sequential accumulation, so implementation precision per se is not a contract violation — only exceeding the 1% bound matters.", "No test harness code is present in the artifact (test_code empty); verification must construct its own float64 reference from make_inputs_numpy()."], "open_questions": ["What is the actual fp32-computed alpha vs the float64 alpha on this workload, and does the resulting residual error direction differ from the reference by more than 1% relative L2?", "Does the final output remain finite (norm > 0 in fp32) on this workload?", "How large is the cancellation effect in practice: are residual components ~1e-5 with ~5 digits retained, or does the systematic alpha error dominate?"], "summary": "Described case_p: fp32 Triton kernel computing a normalized orthogonal projection residual for a fixed seeded (32,) workload where b = 1.125*u + 1e-5*noise, making residual cancellation in fp32 the central correctness risk."}
